subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of the hyperbola whose foci are (±5, 0) and whose transverse axis has length 8.

mark_split.label: Find b and write the equation

insider_note: Foci on the x-axis with the transverse-axis length also given (not eccentricity) is the fastest route: get a first from 2a, then e = (given ae)/a, then b² last — trying to find b² before a wastes time.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find a and e
steps.margin_note: First mark. The axis length gives a directly; the foci then give e.
steps.memory_tip: Transverse axis LENGTH is 2a, not a — halve it first.
steps.why: The foci give ae directly, and the transverse-axis length gives a on its own — dividing the two recovers e without needing b at all yet.
common_mistakes: Using 2a = 8 to say a = 8 instead of a = 4 — the axis length is 2a, not a.
Mixing up ae = 5 (from the foci) with a itself.

steps.label: Find b and write the equation
steps.margin_note: Second mark. b² = a²(e²−1), never a²(1−e²) as for an ellipse.
steps.memory_tip: For a hyperbola e > 1, so e² − 1 is always positive — the ellipse formula a²(1−e²) would give a NEGATIVE number here, a sure sign of using the wrong formula.

lines.text: Equation of the hyperbola: x²/16 − y²/9 = 1

steps.why: b² is found from the identity b² = a²(e²−1), which comes from e² = (a²+b²)/a² rearranged; once a² and b² are known the standard form follows directly.
common_mistakes: Using b² = a²(1−e²) — the ellipse formula — instead of the hyperbola's b² = a²(e²−1); for a hyperbola e>1 so e²−1 is positive, giving a positive b².
Forgetting to square a before substituting into the standard form (writing x²/4 instead of x²/16).
